checks: The avatars bucket is public, limited to 100 KB, and takes only WebP and JPEG
Anonymous cannot ask for an upload place
Anonymous cannot save a photo
Only WebP and JPEG places are issued
An active user gets an upload place and the limit
The place is chosen by the server inside the caller's folder
A JPEG place ends in .jpg
A place with no stored file cannot be saved
Another account cannot store a file in someone's place
A place the server did not issue cannot be used
The bucket refuses a file over 100 KB
The bucket refuses other image types
The owner stores the photo in the issued place
A stored photo cannot be replaced
The photo is readable at its public address without signing in
Nobody can list the bucket, the owner included
Nobody can delete a photo file through the app session
Another account cannot claim the upload
Rejected attempts leave no photo
A stored, issued file is saved as the photo path
An upload cannot be applied twice
The stored size is recorded
The owner reads their photo path
An unrelated patient cannot read the path
An unlinked therapist cannot read the path
A linked therapist reads the path through the patient list
The owner cannot write the photo column directly
Only Motivance photo paths can be stored, even by the database owner
WebP is the default type
A new photo replaces the old one
The replaced photo is marked for removal
The administrator directory includes the photo
A therapist cannot use photo moderation
An administrator removes a photo
The moderated photo is cleared
Moderation is audited with the administrator as actor
The owner removes their own photo
Upload places are limited to ten an hour
Photo changes are audited
Only the service key can list photos due for removal
Replaced, moderated and removed photos are due for removal
The cleanup removes the files from Storage
A removed photo is no longer reachable at its address
Removed photos are not tried again
environment: real local Auth, PostgREST and Storage; disposable users
limitations: Image content is not inspected by the server; type and size are enforced from the upload headers and the bucket.
